questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: An equiconvex lens of focal length $f$, is cut into four parts as shown in the diagram. The focal length of each part is
questions.solution: For an equiconvex lens, focal length $f = \frac{R}{2(\mu - 1)}$. When cut vertically and horizontally into four equal parts, each part acts as a plano-convex lens with focal length $f' = \frac{R}{\mu - 1} = 2f$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Radius of a tube decreases from $2R$ to $R$ in which ideal liquid is flowing at same level. Speed at one end is $2\text{ m/s}$ as shown, find speed $v$ at other end.
questions.solution: By equation of continuity: $A_1 v_1 = A_2 v_2 \implies \pi (2R)^2 \cdot 2 = \pi R^2 v \implies v = 8\text{ m/s}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The dimensional formula of capacitance is
questions.solution: Energy stored in a capacitor $E = \frac{Q^2}{2C} \implies C = \frac{Q^2}{2E}$. Dimensions: $[C] = \frac{[\text{A}^2\text{T}^2]}{[\text{M}\text{L}^2\text{T}^{-2}]} = [\text{M}^{-1}\text{L}^{-2}\text{T}^4\text{A}^2]$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A proton is moving with uniform velocity of $2 \times 10^8\text{ m/s}$ in uniform magnetic and electric fields which are perpendicular to each other. If electric field is switched off then proton moves in circular path of radius $1.6 \times 10^{-5}\text{ m}$. Then magnetic field $B$ is
questions.solution: Radius of circular path in magnetic field is $r = \frac{mv}{qB} \implies 1.6 \times 10^{-5} = \frac{1.6 \times 10^{-27} \times 2 \times 10^8}{1.6 \times 10^{-19} \times B} \implies B = \frac{5}{4} \times 10^5 = 1.25 \times 10^5\text{ T} \approx 1.2 \times 10^5\text{ T}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A conducting circular ring is moving with a constant velocity in a uniform magnetic field as shown. Identify the correct graph between induced emf vs time.
questions.solution: Induced emf $\delta = 2Bv\sqrt{R^2 - x^2}$ where $x = R - vt$. This represents an elliptical profile for entry into and exit from the magnetic field, corresponding to Graph (1).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The displacement of a particle moving under the action of a force $\vec{F} = 2\hat{i} + b\hat{j} + \hat{k}$ is $\vec{d} = \hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}$. Find the value of $b$ if the work done by the force is zero.
questions.solution: Work done $= \vec{F} \cdot \vec{d} = (2\hat{i} + b\hat{j} + \hat{k}) \cdot (\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}) = 2 + b + 1 = 3 + b = 0 \implies b = -3$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: In a series LCR circuit the maximum amplitude of current is $I_0$ when the resistance is $R$. What is the maximum amplitude of current if the resistor is replaced by a resistor of resistance $\frac{R}{2}$?
questions.solution: Current has maximum amplitude at resonance, $I_0 = \frac{\xi_0}{R}$. When $R$ is replaced by $R/2$, $I_0' = \frac{\xi_0}{R/2} = 2I_0$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
Statement-I : Fringe width of red light is more than fringe width of violet light.
Statement-II : Fringe width is directly proportional to the wavelength of light used.
Choose the correct option.
options: Statement-I is correct and statement-II is incorrect
Both statement-I and statement-II are correct
Statement-I is incorrect and statement-II is correct
Both statement-I and statement-II are incorrect
questions.solution: Fringe width $\beta = \frac{\lambda D}{d}$. Since wavelength of red light $\lambda_{\text{red}} > \lambda_{\text{violet}}$, fringe width of red light is greater. Both statement-I and statement-II are correct.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: For non-vibrating diatomic gas has adiabatic constant of $\gamma_1$ & for vibrating diatomic gas has adiabatic constant of $\gamma_2$ then
questions.solution: For non-vibrating diatomic gas, degrees of freedom $f=5 \implies \gamma_1 = 1 + \frac{2}{5} = 1.4$. For vibrating diatomic gas, $f=7 \implies \gamma_2 = 1 + \frac{2}{7} = 1.28$. Therefore $\gamma_1 > \gamma_2$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A force $\vec{F} = (\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - 3\hat{k})\text{ N}$ acts on point whose position vector is given as $\vec{r} = (2\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + 7\hat{k})\text{ m}$. Find torque about origin.
questions.solution: Torque $\vec{\tau} = \vec{r} \times \vec{F} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 2 & -3 & 7 \\ 1 & 2 & -3 \end{vmatrix} = \hat{i}(9-14) - \hat{j}(-6-7) + \hat{k}(4+3) = -5\hat{i} + 13\hat{j} + 7\hat{k}\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The net magnetic field at point O due to the two infinite current carrying wires shown in the figure is
questions.solution: $B_{\text{net}} = \frac{\mu_0 (4\text{ A})}{2\pi (4\text{ cm})} - \frac{\mu_0 (5\text{ A})}{2\pi (10\text{ cm})} = \frac{25 \mu_0}{\pi} = 10^{-5}\text{ T}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
Read the statements and select the correct option.
Statement I : A pendulum is taken from Earth to another planet having mass four times and radius double than earth, then time period of pendulum remain same as on earth.
Statement II : The time period of pendulum only depends on the gravity of the planet.
options: Statement I is true but statement II is false.
Statement II is true but statement I is false.
questions.solution: On another planet, $g' = \frac{G(4M)}{(2R)^2} = g$, so time period remains same. Statement II is false because $T = 2\pi \sqrt{l/g}$ depends on length $l$ as well as $g$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
For a given logic circuit truth table is given, identify the gate G.
Truth Table:
$A=0, B=0 \implies y=1$
$A=1, B=0 \implies y=0$
$A=0, B=1 \implies y=0$
$A=1, B=1 \implies y=1$
questions.solution: From the truth table, the circuit represents an XNOR gate ($y = \bar{A}\bar{B} + AB$). Therefore, the output gate G must be a NOR gate.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Name the logic gate shown in the circuit diagram.
questions.solution: If both inputs A and B are high only then output Y is high, otherwise Y is low. Hence it is an AND Gate.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Displacement current in capacitor of area $16\text{ cm}^2$ is $6\text{ A}$ at an instant. Find displacement current across area $3.2\text{ cm}^2$
questions.solution: $i_d = \epsilon_0 A \frac{dE}{dt} \implies i_d \propto A$. Therefore $i' = \left(\frac{3.2}{16}\right) \times 6\text{ A} = 1.2\text{ A}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: In the RC circuit shown, find $I$.
questions.solution: At steady state, C behaves as an open-circuit. The equivalent resistance of the resistor network is $R_{\text{eq}} = \frac{13}{8}R$. Thus $I = \frac{V}{R_{\text{eq}}} = \frac{8V}{13R}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A glass slab of refractive index $\mu_g = 1.44$ is coated with a thin film of refractive index $\mu_f = 2$. The minimum thickness of the film so that maximum transmission of green light of wavelength $\lambda = 5000\text{ \AA}$ (incident normally) takes place is
questions.solution: For maximum transmission of light incident normally, $2\mu_f t = n\lambda$. For $n=1$, minimum thickness $t_{\text{min}} = \frac{\lambda}{2\mu_f} = \frac{5000 \times 10^{-10}}{2 \times 2}\text{ m} = 0.125\text{ }\mu\text{m}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: For the electric dipole shown in the figure, the electric field and the electric potential are $E_0, V_0$ at a distance $r$ on the axis. Then what is the electric field and the electric potential at a point on the equatorial plane at a distance $2r$?
questions.solution: $E_{\text{axis}} = \frac{2kP}{r^3} = E_0$. $E_{\text{equatorial}} = \frac{kP}{(2r)^3} = \frac{kP}{8r^3} = \frac{E_0}{16}$. $V_{\text{equatorial}} = \frac{kP\cos 90^\circ}{(2r)^2} = 0$.

questions.text: Toluene reacts with $\text{CrO}_2\text{Cl}_2$ in $\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}_2$, followed by $\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$ to give B, which on reaction with $\text{NaHSO}_3$ gives the product. The product is:

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Arrange according to CFSE.
(i) $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$
(ii) $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$
(iii) $[\text{Co(NH}_3)_6]^{2+}$
(iv) $[\text{Co(en)}_3]^{3+}$
questions.solution: CFSE $\propto$ charge on central metal ion and $\propto$ ligand field strength. Thus, $[\text{Co(en)}_3]^{3+} > [\text{Co(NH}_3)_6]^{3+} > [\text{Co(NH}_3)_6]^{2+} > [\text{Co(NH}_3)_4]^{2+}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
What is correct order of stability of carbocation?
(a) $p-\text{CH}_3\text{O}-\text{C}_6\text{H}_4-\text{CH}_2^+$
(b) $p-\text{CH}_3-\text{C}_6\text{H}_4-\text{CH}_2^+$
(c) $m-\text{OMe}-\text{C}_6\text{H}_4-\text{CH}_2^+$
(d) $m-\text{CH}_3-\text{C}_6\text{H}_4-\text{CH}_2^+$
questions.solution: Carbocation stability depends on $+M, HC, +I$ effects. (a) has $+M$ effect, (b) has hyperconjugation, (c) has $-I$ effect of OMe at meta position, (d) has $+I$ effect.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Which of the following anion will not undergo disproportionation?
questions.solution: In $\text{ClO}_4^-$, chlorine is in its highest oxidation state (+7), so it cannot undergo disproportionation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Compare dipole moment of
(I) $\text{NF}_3$ (II) $\text{CHCl}_3$ (III) $\text{H}_2\text{S}$ (IV) $\text{HBr}$
questions.solution: Dipole moment values: $\text{CHCl}_3 (1.04\text{ D}) > \text{H}_2\text{S} (0.95\text{ D}) > \text{HBr} (0.79\text{ D}) > \text{NF}_3 (0.230\text{ D})$. Thus order is II > III > IV > I.

S-II: Lassaigne extract is made with magnesium metal.
options: Both S-I and S-II are correct.
Both S-I and S-II are incorrect.
S-I is correct but S-II is incorrect.

questions.solution: Lassaigne extract is prepared using sodium metal, not magnesium metal. Statement I is correct, Statement II is incorrect.

questions.solution: In 3-ethyl-2,2-dimethylpentane, the number of secondary hydrogen ($2^\circ H$) atoms is 2.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Secondary butyl cyclohexane when reacts with $\text{Br}_2$ in presence of sunlight produce
questions.solution: Free radical bromination occurs preferentially at the tertiary carbon of the cyclohexane ring to give 1-bromo-1-sec-butylcyclohexane as the major product.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: $200\text{ mL}$ of $0.2\text{ M}$ solution of $\text{NaOH}$ is mixed with $400\text{ mL}$ of $0.5\text{ M}$ $\text{NaOH}$ solution. Molarity of mixture is
questions.solution: Molarity of mixture $= \frac{M_1 V_1 + M_2 V_2}{V_1 + V_2} = \frac{0.2 \times 200 + 0.5 \times 400}{200 + 400} = \frac{40 + 200}{600} = 0.4\text{ M}$.

options: Fischer projection with -CHO top, -CH2OH bottom, -H left, -OH right
Fischer projection with -CH2OH top, -CHO bottom, -HO left, -H right
Fischer projection with -CH2OH top, -CHO bottom, -H left, -OH right
Fischer projection with -CH2OH top, -CHO right, -OH bottom
questions.solution: In standard Fischer projection, L-Glyceraldehyde has $-\text{OH}$ group on the left side of the chiral carbon.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Identify the extensive and intensive property?
options: Mass, temperature, heat, volume – Extensive property
Mass, volume, internal energy – Extensive property
Density, temperature, moles, internal energy – Intensive property
questions.solution: Mass, volume and internal energy depend on the amount of matter present in the system, hence they are extensive properties.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Among Group-15 elements, what is the maximum covalency of an element having weakest E–E bond (E = element)
questions.solution: Bond energies of Group 15 E-E bonds: N-N (167 kJ/mol), P-P (201 kJ/mol), As-As (146 kJ/mol), Sb-Sb (121 kJ/mol). Sb has the weakest bond, and its maximum covalency is 5.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: What is the relation between $K_{sp}$ and $S$ of $\text{Zr}_3(\text{PO}_4)_4$
questions.solution: $\text{Zr}_3(\text{PO}_4)_4(s) \rightleftharpoons 3\text{Zr}^{4+}(aq) + 4\text{PO}_4^{3-}(aq)$. $K_{sp} = (3S)^3 (4S)^4 = 27 \times 256 S^7 = 6912 S^7 \implies S = \left(\frac{K_{sp}}{6912}\right)^{1/7}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text:
Match the column and choose the correct option.
(A) $\left(\frac{\partial H}{\partial T}\right)_P$
(B) $\left(\frac{\partial G}{\partial P}\right)_T$
(C) $\left(\frac{\partial U}{\partial T}\right)_V$
(D) $\left(\frac{\partial G}{\partial T}\right)_P$

Options list:
(P) $C_P$, (Q) $C_V$, (R) $-S$, (S) $V$
questions.solution: Thermodynamic relations: $\left(\frac{\partial H}{\partial T}\right)_P = C_P$, $\left(\frac{\partial G}{\partial P}\right)_T = V$, $\left(\frac{\partial U}{\partial T}\right)_V = C_V$, $\left(\frac{\partial G}{\partial T}\right)_P = -S$.

S-1 : During corrosion pure metal acts as anode and impure metal acts as cathode.
S-2 : Rate of corrosion is more in alkaline medium than in acidic medium.
options: Both S-1 and S-2 are correct
Both S-1 and S-2 are incorrect
S-1 is correct but S-2 is incorrect
S-1 is incorrect but S-2 is correct
questions.solution: In corrosion, metal acts as anode where oxidation occurs. Rate of corrosion is higher in acidic medium due to the availability of $H^+$ ions. Both statements are incorrect.

questions.solution: The complex formed is $[\text{Ni(DMG)}_2]$, which has 2 intramolecular hydrogen bonds in its structure.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: $\text{R-Br} + \text{Mg} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \text{A} \xrightarrow{\text{H}_2\text{O}} \text{isopentane}$. How many $\text{R-Br}$ can form isopentane?
questions.solution: Isopentane is $(CH_3)_2CHCH_2CH_3$. Bromine can be attached at 4 different carbons to form alkyl bromides that yield isopentane upon hydrolysis of Grignard reagent.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: $\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 \xrightarrow{\text{Monobromination}} \text{Single product}$, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 \xrightarrow[Cat.]{\text{4 moles of }\text{H}_2} \text{Completely hydrogenated product}$. Find the number of $\pi$-electrons in $\text{C}_6\text{H}_6$.
questions.solution: Degree of unsaturation of $\text{C}_6\text{H}_6 = 4$. Since it consumes 4 moles of $\text{H}_2$ and gives a single monobrominated product, it is a symmetrical dialkyne (hex-1,5-diyne). Number of $\pi$-electrons $= 4 \times 2 = 8$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: Calculate the radius of first excited state of $\text{He}^+$ ion (in \AA)
questions.solution: Radius $r = a_0 \frac{n^2}{Z}$. For first excited state of $\text{He}^+$, $n = 2, Z = 2 \implies r = a_0 \frac{4}{2} = 2 a_0 = 2 \times 0.529 = 1.058\text{ \AA} \approx 1\text{ \AA}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If $2x^2 + (\cos\theta)x - 1 = 0$, $\theta \in [0, 2\pi]$ has roots $\alpha$ and $\beta$. Then the sum of maximum and minimum value of $\alpha^4 + \beta^4$.
questions.solution: $\alpha + \beta = \frac{-\cos\theta}{2}, \alpha\beta = -1/2$. $\alpha^2 + \beta^2 = (\alpha+\beta)^2 - 2\alpha\beta = \frac{\cos^2\theta+4}{4}$. $\alpha^4 + \beta^4 = (\alpha^2+\beta^2)^2 - 2\alpha^2\beta^2 = \left(\frac{\cos^2\theta+4}{4}\right)^2 - \frac{1}{2}$. Minimum value (at $\cos\theta=0$) is $1 - 1/2 = 1/2$. Maximum value (at $\cos\theta=1$) is $25/16 - 1/2 = 17/16$. Sum $= 1/2 + 17/16 = 25/16$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If $\theta \in [0, 2\pi]$ satisfying the system of equations $2\sin^2\theta = \cos 2\theta$ and $2\cos 2\theta = 3\sin\theta$. Then the sum of all real values of $\theta$ is
questions.solution: Adding the equations: $2 = 1 - 2\sin^2\theta + 3\sin\theta \implies 2\sin^2\theta - 3\sin\theta + 1 = 0 \implies (2\sin\theta - 1)(\sin\theta - 1) = 0$. $\sin\theta = 1$ is not consistent with $2\sin^2\theta = \cos 2\theta$. Thus $\sin\theta = 1/2 \implies \theta = \frac{\pi}{6}, \frac{5\pi}{6}$. Sum $= \frac{\pi}{6} + \frac{5\pi}{6} = \pi$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let $A = \{1, 2, 3, 4\}$ and $B = \{1, 4, 9, 16\}$. If $f : A \rightarrow B$, number of many-one functions from $A$ to $B$ are
questions.solution: Total number of functions $= 4^4 = 256$. Number of one-one functions $= 4! = 24$. Number of many-one functions $= 256 - 24 = 232$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: 4 boys and 3 girls are to be seated in a row such that all girls seat together and two particular boys $B_1$ and $B_2$ are not adjacent to each other. Then the number of ways in which this arrangement can be done.
questions.solution: Treat 3 girls as a single unit. The 3 girls and remaining 2 boys can be seated in $3! \times 3! = 36$ ways. $B_1$ and $B_2$ can be placed into the 4 available spaces in ${}^4P_2 = 12$ ways. Total ways $= 36 \times 12 = 432$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Consider a function $f(x) = \int_0^{x^2} \frac{t^2 - 8t + 15}{e^t} dt$. The number of points of extrema are
questions.solution: Using Leibniz rule: $f'(x) = \frac{2x(x^4 - 8x^2 + 15)}{e^{x^2}} = \frac{2x(x^2-5)(x^2-3)}{e^{x^2}}$. Critical points are $x = 0, \pm\sqrt{5}, \pm\sqrt{3}$. Thus there are 5 points of extrema.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let $A$ and $B$ are two events such that $P(A \cap B) = \frac{1}{10}$ and $P(A/B)$ and $P(B/A)$ are the roots of the equation $12x^2 - 7x + 1 = 0$, then $\frac{P(\bar{A} \cup \bar{B})}{P(\bar{A} \cap \bar{B})}$ is equal to
questions.solution: $12x^2 - 7x + 1 = 0 \implies x = 1/3, 1/4$. $P(A/B) + P(B/A) = 7/12$. $P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B) = 6/10$. $\frac{P(\bar{A} \cup \bar{B})}{P(\bar{A} \cap \bar{B})} = \frac{1 - P(A \cap B)}{1 - P(A \cup B)} = \frac{9/10}{4/10} = \frac{9}{4}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Number of terms in an arithmetic progression is $2n$. Sum of terms occurring at even places is 40 and sum of terms occurring at odd places is 55. If the first term exceeds the last term by 27, then $n$ equals to
questions.solution: Sum at even places: $na + n^2 d = 40$. Sum at odd places: $na + dn(n-1) = 55$. Subtracting gives $nd = -15$. Given $a - (a + (2n-1)d) = 27 \implies -(2n-1)d = 27 \implies d = \frac{-27}{2n-1}$. Thus $-n \left(\frac{-27}{2n-1}\right) = 15 \implies 27n = 30n - 15 \implies n = 5$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The perpendicular distance of point $P(3, 4, 5)$ from the line $\vec{r} = 2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k} + \lambda(4\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 5\hat{k})$ is
questions.solution: Any point $A$ on line is $(2+4\lambda, -1-\lambda, 1+5\lambda)$. $\vec{AP} \cdot (4\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 5\hat{k}) = 0 \implies 16\lambda - 4 + \lambda + 5 + 25\lambda - 20 = 0 \implies 42\lambda = 19 \implies \lambda = 19/42$. Distance $|AP| = \sqrt{\frac{19}{42}}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: In the expansion of $\left(x + \sqrt{x^3-1}\right)^5 + \left(x - \sqrt{x^3-1}\right)^5$, where $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ and $\delta$ are the coefficient of $x, x^3, x^5$ and $x^7$ respectively. If $\alpha u - \beta v = 18, \gamma u + \delta v = 20$ then $u + v$ equal to
questions.solution: Expansion $= 2[x^5 + 10x^3(x^3-1) + 5x(x^3-1)^2] = 10x^7 + 20x^6 + 2x^5 - 20x^4 - 20x^3 + 10x$. Coefficients: $\alpha = 10, \beta = -20, \gamma = 2, \delta = 10$. Equations: $10u + 20v = 18$ and $2u + 10v = 20 \implies u = -11/3, v = 41/15 \implies u+v = -14/15$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let $A(6, 8), B(10\cos\alpha, -10\sin\alpha)$ and $C(-10\sin\alpha, -10\cos\alpha)$ be 3 points and if orthocentre of the triangle $ABC$ is $(0, 9)$ then $100\sin^2\alpha$ is equal to
questions.solution: Circumcentre $O = (0,0)$. Centroid $G$ divides $HO$ in $2:1$ ratio. $y_G = \frac{8 - 10\sin\alpha - 10\cos\alpha}{3} = 3 \implies 10(\sin\alpha+\cos\alpha) = -1$. $x_G = \frac{6 + 10\cos\alpha - 10\sin\alpha}{3} = 0 \implies 10(\sin\alpha-\cos\alpha) = -6$. Adding gives $20\sin\alpha = -5 \implies 100\sin^2\alpha = 25/4$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If $z$ be a complex number such that $|z - 3| \le 1$, then the equation of line with largest slope passing through origin and $z$
questions.solution: Maximum slope line is tangent to the circle $|z-3| = 1$. $\tan\theta = \frac{1}{\sqrt{8}} = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}$. Equation is $y = \frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}x \implies x - 2\sqrt{2}y = 0$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A relation $R$ is defined on set $A, A = \{1, 2, 3\}$ and $R = \{(1, 2), (2, 3)\}$. Elements are added such that $R$ becomes reflexive and transitive but not symmetric. Find the number of such relations.
questions.solution: For $R$ to be reflexive, $(1,1), (2,2), (3,3)$ must be added. For transitivity, $(1,3)$ must be added. The remaining pairs $(2,1), (3,2), (3,1)$ can be added selectively without creating symmetry. Exactly 3 valid relations are possible.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ be two unit vectors such that angle between $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ is $\frac{\pi}{3}$. If $\lambda \vec{a} + 3\vec{b}$ and $2\vec{a} + \lambda \vec{b}$ are perpendicular to each other, then the product of all possible values of $\lambda$ is ____
questions.solution: $(\lambda \vec{a} + 3\vec{b}) \cdot (2\vec{a} + \lambda \vec{b}) = 0 \implies 2\lambda + 3\lambda + (\lambda^2+6)\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b} = 0 \implies 5\lambda + (\lambda^2+6)(1/2) = 0 \implies \lambda^2 + 10\lambda + 6 = 0$. Product of possible values of $\lambda = 6$.

questions.text: Consider two curves $E_1 : \frac{x^2}{a^2} + \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 1$ with eccentricity $e_1$ and $E_2 : \frac{x^2}{A^2} + \frac{y^2}{B^2} = 1$ with eccentricity $e_2$. If $\frac{e_1}{e_2} = \frac{1}{3}$ and distance between foci of both curves is $2\sqrt{3}$ and $a - A = 4$, then the sum of lengths of latus rectum of both curves is
questions.solution: $2ae_1 = 2\sqrt{3} = 2Ae_2 \implies ae_1 = Ae_2$. Since $e_1/e_2 = 1/3 \implies a = 3A$. Given $a - A = 4 \implies A = 2, a = 6$. $e_1 = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{6} \implies b^2 = 33$. $e_2 = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \implies B^2 = 1$. Latus rectum sum $= \frac{2b^2}{a} + \frac{2B^2}{A} = \frac{2(33)}{6} + \frac{2(1)}{2} = 11 + 1 = 12$.

questions.text: The number of maximum number of common tangents to the curves $y = (x - 2)^2$ and $y^2 = 16 - 8x$ is
questions.solution: Plotting both parabolas, $y = (x-2)^2$ opening upwards with vertex at $(2,0)$ and $y^2 = -8(x-2)$ opening leftwards with vertex at $(2,0)$. They touch at $(2,0)$, giving exactly 1 common tangent.
